about: The lanes of Python CI (.github/workflows/python-app.yml) and the durations they are balanced on. tests/test_repository_config.py holds the workflow to the lanes, each lane with the allowance for each link to the bound, each job that starts with the run to its measured length, and each job that waits on another to an artifact it reads.

parallel_jobs.tests: the critical path of a run
parallel_jobs.minimum-versions: the suite at the dependency floors
parallel_jobs.doc-snippets: runs every snippet of the documentation
parallel_jobs.remote-node: builds the node image and runs the simulations on it
parallel_jobs.mps: holds a macOS runner, whose cap of five the test legs fill, so a link queued behind them would wait out a whole test leg

parallel_about: A job starts with the run when it holds a macOS runner, or when its shortest measured run takes longer than a quarter of lane_bound_s, so a short job cannot leave its lane.

after_jobs.release-rebuild-macos: reads the release-checksums artifact of release-build
after_jobs.sonar: reads the coverage that tests uploads
after_jobs.pr-comment: reads the test results that tests uploads

after_about: A job waits on another only to read an artifact that a job it waits on uploads.
scope_about: The job every job that can skip waits on, for the jobs no changed file reaches (scripts/ci_scope.py). It waits on nothing and takes seconds; a wait on it is no place in the lanes.

measured.about: Seconds from start to end of each job in run 44207513864 (pull request 1158, green) and run 44207512197 (pull request 1157, whose short jobs all ended green but whose macOS test legs and macOS rebuild never started, so the run did not finish), with every job still starting with the run, and in run 44228030331 (pull request 1161, green), the first with the lanes. A lane counts the longest run of each link; a job that starts with the run counts the shortest, and a matrix its shortest leg that ran.

link_waits_s.about: The queue wait, from creation to start, of each job created when the jobs it waits on ended, which is what a lane link goes through: sonar and pr-comment of each run that reached them (run 44207512197 never did); the links of the lanes are under lane_runs. The 21 Ubuntu jobs created with run 44207513864 waited 10 s to 795 s, median 302 s, but those waits come from 28 jobs queued at once and say nothing of a link queued later.

link_allowance_about: The wait of a link for its runner once the one before it ends: at least the longest wait measured for a job queued after the jobs it waits on ended (175 s, sonar in run 44207513864), and in each run with the lanes at least what the links of a lane waited, shared among them.

lane_runs.about: Runs with the lanes. For each lane, the queue wait from creation to start of each link after the head, and the seconds from the start of the run to the end of its last link. In run 44228030331 (pull request 1161) the first link of each lane waited while the 19 jobs that start with the run took their runners (152 s and 238 s), and every later link waited 2 s to 11 s.

tests_matrix_wall_s.about: The longest leg of the test matrix, start to end, in each run: the time the matrix holds its last runner.

lane_bound_about: Two thirds of the shortest matrix measured, so a lane ends well before the tests and never becomes the critical path.
